newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia coalition leaders start crisis talks.
newsitem.headline: Estonia coalition leaders start crisis talks.

text.p: Estonia's governing coalition leaders held crisis talks on Friday after the prime minister and foreign minister clashed in hefty campaigning for local elections held last weekend.

Siim Kallas, Minister of Foreign Affairs and chairman of the coalition's Reform Party, and Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi, head of the Coalition Party, have been haggling publicly in the media over the last week.

The two met other government members at the government residence outside the capital in a bid to resolve their differences, which analysts said seemed to lie more with personalities than policy issues.
Estonian radio quoted Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi as saying that the conflict "has everything to do with the local elections", which both coalition partners fought vigorously.

Vaehi has complained that Kallas in electioneering was "publicly seeking the prime minister's post", and Kallas after the poll sought to capitalise on the slight gains his party made in the local vote.
Vaehi said on Friday snap elections would probably not change the composition of the current parliament, so there would be little point in bringing the government down.
Both men were non-committal as they started their meeting: "We have always been very straightforward, I think we will have clear talks but that's all I can say," said Vaehi.

Government crises have been endemic in Estonia since it quit the former Soviet Union in 1991 but administrations have always kept the country on the path of economic reform, and the current three-party coalition has held together since October 1995.
